title: Design an Image Reconstruction Service
interviewAnswer: For heavy image/3D inference, prefer asynchronous job submission: upload input, validate, enqueue work, run GPU inference, store outputs, expose job status, and monitor latency/failures/quality.
why: Image reconstruction system design tests how you turn a heavy research model into a reliable service with storage, GPU scheduling and asynchronous workflows.
intuition: Separate upload/job orchestration from GPU inference. Long-running reconstruction should be a queued job with status/result storage, not a blocking request.
deepDive: Validate input file/shape/version, store raw input in object storage, create a job record, queue work, run preprocessing+versioned model in a GPU worker/container, write outputs/quality metrics, update status and expose results. Add retries that are idempotent, resource limits, checkpoint/model cache, access control and lifecycle cleanup for huge 3D artifacts.
workedExample: 64³ volume upload → API returns job_id → GPU worker loads CycleGAN checkpoints → three-plane Stage1/interpolation/refinement/fusion → 1024³ raw result stored → UI shows completion/download path.
commonMistakes: Passing multi-GB volume bytes repeatedly between services instead of object-storage references.
Not versioning the exact preprocessing/model pair.
followUps: How do you scale GPU workers?
How do you handle failed jobs?
production: Monitor queue wait, GPU utilization, stage timing, failure reasons, output quality and storage cost; use immutable job/model metadata for reproducibility.
